newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
CONGRESS CHIEF'S SUPPORTERS INTENSIFY CAMPAIGN

Congress president Sitaram Kesri's supporters have intensified their efforts to evolve a consensus in his favour for the post of Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) leader. Kesri supporters held a series of meetings to devise a strategy to elect the CPP leader without leaving any bitterness in the party. Since the election would be held on January 3, it was decided to use the available time press for a consensus. Meanwhile, Congress Working Committee member Rajesh Pilot insisted that he would be a candidate for the election of CPP leader.
The Pioneer
EVICTION ORDERS FOR GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES

The Supreme Court ordered eviction of over 2,000 government employees who were allotted out-of-turn accommodation in New Delhi under the discretionary quota of the housing ministry. The court said all these employees should be issued notices within 30 days and they must vacate their houses within 90 days thereafter. The court also ordered that the government's discretionary quota must not exceed more than five percent of houses in all categories every year.
The Economic Times
PROPOSAL ON 100 PCT BOOK BUILDING PUT ON HOLD

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) proposal to allow 100 percent book building in equity issues has been stalled by its governing board. The board felt that this would inhibit the right of the investors to apply for an issue. The board felt if public issues were allowed through the wholly book building route then the entire issue would be the prerogative of the lead managers or book runners, who would then be free to distribute it in the manner they deemed fit.
DUTCH MAJOR TO BUY 51 PCT STAKE IN ALPHA DRUGS

The Dutch pharmaceutical and chemical giant, DSM, is taking over Alpha Drugs of Patiala. The Dutch major will acquire a 51 percent stake in Alpha Drugs, the country's biggest producer of D-alpha phenyl glycine derivatives, key inputs in penicillin-based products. DSM already holds 15 percent in Alpha. After the takeover, the company's name is expected to be changed to DSM India Ltd.
Financial Express
BANK OF BARODA REDUCES PLR TO 14.5 PCT

The Bank of Baroda (BoB) slashed its prime lending rate by 50 basis points to bring it down to 14.5 percent at par with the State Bank of India (SBI), Corporation Bank and Union Bank. BoB, the largest Indian bank after SBI, also brought down the interest rate band by 50 basis points to three percent. With this, the bank capped the maximum interest rate at 17.5 percent, the lowest among all public sector banks.
STAKE IN REGIONAL RURAL BANKS MAY BE SOLD

The government may divest its stake in some of the regional rural banks (RRBs) in favour of the promoters of the proposed local area banks (LABs). Finance Minister P. Chidambaram mooted the concept of LABs in his Budget speech this year. The government presently holds 50 percent stake in RRBs. The complicated holding pattern is one of the major hurdles that comes in the way of restructuring the RRBs. The finance ministry feels the idea of selling the government stake to the promoters of local area banks is likely to be welcomed as the promoters would get ready infrastructure.
Business Standard
UK CORPORATION KEEN ON INVESTMENT IN PORTS

The Commonwealth Development Corporation (CDC), a UK-based overseas development finance institution, has decided to focus on India for investment in the port sector. Although no specific sum has been earmarked, the corporation may invest as much as 1.4 billion rupees in financing and developing a single port. The financial institution is planning to invest in major as well as minor ports. CDC's plans to invest in the port sector is part of its overall strategy to record a quantum jump in its investment in India from the current level of nine billion rupees to over 20 billion rupees in next four years.
The Observer
FINANCE MINISTER ALLAYS RECESSION FEARS

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said apprehensions about an economic recession, being talked of by the industry, were highly misplaced. The minister said though low credit offtake, sluggish capital market and other indicators might show an economic slowdown, the fundamentals of the Indian economy continued to be strong. He said exports had grown since last year, the rate of inflation had been successfully pegged at four percent, the rate of change of the consumer price index for the industrial workers had been less than last year's, and the total disbursement by the financial institutions had been 17 percent more than that of the last year.
DUMPING ABOUNDS AS IMPORT DUTY FALLS

India is becoming a dumping ground for foreign sellers with falling import duties. The Designated Authority of Anti-dumping, the commerce ministry's arm to deal with the cases related to dumping, has initiated enquiries against 11 countries for allegedly dumping their products. The cases include nitrile rubber by Germany and South Korea, catalysts by Denmark, acrylic fibre by the U.S., Thailand and South Korea, and graphic electrodes by the U.S., China, Spain, Germany, Italy, France, Belgium and Austria.
CABINET DECISION TODAY ON FDI LIBERALISATION

The Cabinet will meet on Tuesday to approve the industry ministry's proposal to further liberalise foreign direct investment (FDI). The proposal envisages the expansion of the list of industries in which automatic approval of foreign equity up to 51 percent is admissible. The industry ministry has recommended about 25 industries, including those in power, surface transport, port, automobiles, mining, chemicals and food processing, for inclusion in the list of industries for automatic approval of FDI. The proposal to raise the limit on foreign equity from the existing 51 percent to 74 percent for approvals under the automatic route would also come up for a decision at the Cabinet meeting.
